correctness.rationale: For triangle-free G, no pair of neighbors of a vertex are adjacent. Any set of ≥3 neighbors has unique common center by the K2,3-free property; a neighbor pair has a second center exactly when it is the opposite pair of an induced C4. Descending-cardinality pairing F with F∪{v} is a bona fide free-face collapse, since larger cofaces are already gone and all remaining centers are unique. The residual simplices are exactly original graph simplices plus the four triangular faces for each C4, forming one tetrahedral boundary each. Choosing one diagonal for each square gives X_G; the complementary disk attaches along a null-homotopic loop bounding the chosen disk, splitting off one S2. Reconstructed complete free-face operations for 118 valid finite graphs, including Q4, cycles, rectangular grids and random graphs. Finite checks support but do not establish the general theorem.

value.rationale: The structural theorem reduces a natural large simplicial complex to a graph square-cell complex plus one 2-sphere per four-cycle, with an explicit collapse count. It covers arbitrarily large rectangular grids and other cyclic graph configurations without requiring X_G to be contractible, and explains the known hypercube calculation by a broad mechanism. Its invariant and decomposition are intrinsically motivated by the first nontrivial girth-four boundary of an established Čech theory, not a routine substitution or isolated table computation.
